title: Δρυτόμοι καὶ πεύκη
part: The Woodcutters and the Pine (Chambry 100 · Perry 303)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 100 (= Perry 303). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Δρυτόμοι ἔσχιζόν τινα πεύκην· σφῆνας δὲ ἐξ αὐτῆς πεποιηκότες εὐκόλως ἔσχιζον.
sentences.tr: Drytomoi eschizon tina peukēn· sphēnas de ex autēs pepoiēkotes eukolōs eschizon.
sentences.l: Woodcutters were splitting a certain pine; and having made wedges out of it, they went on splitting easily.
sentences.n: The imperfect ἔσχιζον stands at both ends of the sentence, the labour before and the ease after, with the perfect participle πεποιηκότες between them for the act that changed matters. ἐξ αὐτῆς — out of the pine herself — is the whole point of the fable.

sentences.t: Ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· « Οὐ τοσοῦτον τὸν κόψαντα πέλεκυν μέμφομαι ὅσον τοὺς ἐξ ἐμοῦ γεννηθέντας σφῆνας. »
sentences.tr: Hē de eipen· « Ou tosouton ton kopsanta pelekyn memphomai hoson tous ex emou gennēthentas sphēnas. »
sentences.l: And she said: « I do not so much blame the axe that cut me as the wedges begotten out of me. »
sentences.n: ἡ πεύκη is feminine, so the tree speaks as 'she' throughout, and γεννηθέντας makes the wedges her children. τοσοῦτον … ὅσον is the standard correlative pair, 'so much … as'; it returns in the moral.

sentences.t: Ὅτι οὐ τοσοῦτόν ἐστι δεινόν, ὅτε τις ὑπὸ ἀλλοτρίων ἀνθρώπων πάθῃ τι τῶν ἀπαισίων ὅσον ὑπὸ τῶν οἰκείων.
sentences.tr: Hoti ou tosouton esti deinon, hote tis hypo allotriōn anthrōpōn pathēi ti tōn apaisiōn hoson hypo tōn oikeiōn.
sentences.l: That it is not so terrible, when someone suffers some ill-omened thing at the hands of strangers, as at the hands of his own people.
sentences.i: The story shows that it is not so terrible when a man suffers some ill turn at the hands of strangers as at the hands of his own people.
sentences.n: A moral opening with a bare Ὅτι: the introducing verb is unexpressed in the Greek, which begins simply 'That…', and is supplied in the idiomatic line. ἀλλότριοι and οἰκεῖοι are an exact pair — those belonging to another house and those belonging to one's own. τι τῶν ἀπαισίων is a partitive genitive, 'some one of the ill-omened things'. ὅτε with the subjunctive πάθῃ would in classical prose want ἄν (ὅταν); Chambry prints ὅτε, and the sense is the same indefinite 'whenever'.
